scams.name: Rio/São Paulo-to-Paraty Bus & Costa Verde Highway Transfer Overcharge
scams.description:
Paraty sits on the Costa Verde at the kink in the BR-101 between Rio and São Paulo, with no airport of its own. Every visitor arrives by road — 250 km southwest of Rio (a four-hour coach), 340 km northeast of São Paulo (six hours), along a famously winding two-lane highway with 250-plus curves between Angra dos Reis and Paraty itself. That single-route transfer is the lever for 2025's most consistent Paraty markup, worked from Rio's GIG and São Paulo's GRU airport tour-desks, from hotel concierges in both cities, and from WhatsApp 'private apartment owner' contacts that recommend their cousin as the driver.

Real 2026 prices anchor the gap. Costa Verde Transportes runs Rio Novo Rio Rodoviária to Paraty at R$95–R$140 in air-conditioned coaches with reclining seats and an onboard restroom, four to six daily departures, bookable at viacaocostaverde.com.br or buscama.com.br. Reunidas Paulista runs São Paulo Tietê to Paraty at R$130–R$180 over six hours. A legitimate private transfer through BR Transfers, Carioca Transfers, or Litoral Transfers is R$600–R$900 per car (1–4 passengers) Rio–Paraty and R$900–R$1,200 São Paulo–Paraty. The trap quotes start at R$1,800–R$3,000 for a 'private transfer to Paraty' from a GIG or GRU tour-desk (two to three times the real licensed rate), step down to R$1,500 for a hotel-concierge 'recommended driver' kickback, masquerade as a R$350-per-person 'shared shuttle van' that's identical to the R$95 Costa Verde bus at three times the price, and surface as R$2,000 'door-to-door' WhatsApp drivers from your Airbnb owner. Layered on top: a R$80 'taxi to your pousada' quote at Paraty Rodoviária for what's a 5-minute walk or R$20–R$30 metered ride into Centro Histórico, an end-of-trip return-leg quote inflated as urgency ('only R$2,500 available'), an unannounced R$80 'Costa Verde toll surcharge' against actual BR-101 tolls of R$25–R$40, and a R$200 'comfort upgrade van' for motion sickness that turns out to be a regular sedan.

For travellers planning the Rio-Paraty or São Paulo-Paraty leg, the defense is the public coach plus a short Uber to the airport-side terminal. Take Costa Verde Transportes from Rio Novo Rio Rodoviária at R$95–R$140 or Reunidas Paulista from São Paulo Tietê at R$130–R$180 directly to Paraty (book one to two weeks ahead in high season), use a R$60 Uber from GIG to Novo Rio if you're flying into Rio, and refuse every airport tour-desk 'private transfer R$1,800–R$3,000,' every hotel-concierge 'recommended driver R$1,500,' and every 'shared shuttle van R$350 per person' as 2–3× markup over real licensed rates. If you genuinely want a door-to-door private, book BR Transfers, Carioca Transfers, or Litoral Transfers directly at R$600–R$900 per car. At Paraty Rodoviária walk five to ten minutes to Centro Histórico (compact, all attractions within 800 metres) or take a R$20–R$30 local taxi to your pousada. Take Dramamine 30 minutes before boarding for the winding Costa Verde road, plan for daytime travel only (the BR-101 has poor lighting and a serious nighttime accident record), and refuse any 'toll surcharge R$80' since actual round-trip tolls are R$25–R$40.
scams.avoidance: Costa Verde Transportes bus Novo Rio-Paraty R$95–R$140 (book direct) From GIG: Uber R$60 to Novo Rio + bus = R$155–R$200 total Private door-to-door: BR Transfers / Carioca / Litoral R$600–R$900 At Paraty Rodoviária, walk 5–10 min to Centro Histórico Take Dramamine 30 min before — winding 250-curve Costa Verde road
scams.location: Rio Novo Rio bus terminal (Costa Verde routes), São Paulo Tietê bus terminal, Costa Verde BR-101 highway, GIG / GRU airport tour-desk transfer counters, Paraty Rodoviária
scams.tldr: Paraty has no airport — every traveller arrives via Rio's GIG/SDU (250 km, 4-hour bus) or São Paulo's GRU (340 km, 6-hour bus), where airport tour-desks quote 'private transfer R$1,800–R$3,000' for what costs R$95–R$140 on the Costa Verde Transportes coach and R$600–R$900 on a real private transfer through licensed agencies.

scams.name: Paraty Schooner Boat-Tour Beach-Hopping Overcharge & Unsafe Operators
scams.description:
The Passeio de Escuna — a 5–6 hour wooden-schooner cruise visiting four to six of Paraty Bay's island beaches with snorkelling stops — is the destination's signature excursion and the single biggest visitor activity in the bay. Three reputable operators with consistent Google 4.5+ ratings work the route from Cais do Cabral, Marina, and Pier Largo do Rosário: Saveiros Soberanos, Escuna Mar Aberto, and Escuna Saveiros. The standard product is a 5–6 hour bay loop hitting Lagoa Azul, Praia Vermelha, Ilha Comprida, and Praia da Lula with included snorkel gear, buffet lunch, and soft drinks for R$70–R$120 per person — and the trap menu builds entirely around overselling routes that already exist or putting travellers on unlicensed boats.

Centro Histórico tour-booking touts work the obvious confusion. The most common pitch is 'private schooner R$500 per person' for what's a R$70–R$120 group experience, often with the 'private' boat turning out to be the same group schooner with extra travellers. The 'VIP exclusive route to Lagoa Azul + Praia Vermelha R$800' is fictional — both are standard stops on the public itinerary. The 'all-inclusive open bar premium R$280' is just the standard tour with two extra beers. The 'private islands access R$600' is fiction — Paraty Bay's islands are 95% public-access. Layered on top: R$300 'photo and drone video packages,' a R$50 'mandatory life-jacket rental' on tours where jackets are required-to-be-included safety equipment, and a R$250-per-person 'speedboat to Trindade' from Cais do Cabral pier-front when the actual Trindade route is a R$8 local bus from Paraty Rodoviária plus a R$30–R$60 mini-schooner from Trindade pier itself. The genuine risk sits at unlicensed boats — operators advertising 'cheap schooner R$50 today only' lack life jackets, VHF radios, and Marinha do Brasil registration, and Paraty Bay has documented serious safety incidents during summer afternoon storms.

For travellers planning a Paraty Bay schooner day, the defense is to book directly with a verified Marinha-registered operator and skip every Centro tout. Book the schooner tour only through Google 4.5+ rated operators with verified Marinha do Brasil registration — Saveiros Soberanos at the Marina, Escuna Mar Aberto at Cais do Cabral, or Escuna Saveiros at Pier Largo do Rosário — at R$70–R$120 per person for a 5–6 hour cruise with four to six beach stops, snorkel gear, and lunch included; refuse every dock-front 'private schooner R$500,' 'VIP exclusive route R$800,' 'mid-tour drink package R$200,' and 'life-jacket rental R$50' upsell as either fictional or a violation of safety regulations. Verify life jackets for every passenger before boarding and look for the Marinha registration sticker on the boat. Pre-book one to two days ahead online in the December–February and July high seasons. Confirm the standard four-to-six stops (Lagoa Azul, Praia Vermelha, Ilha Comprida, Praia da Lula) before paying. Bring biodegradable sunscreen only (Paraty Bay reef rules), take Dramamine 30 minutes before for motion sickness and sit centre-boat, and skip the pier-front R$250 'speedboat to Trindade' — the right route is a R$8 bus from Paraty Rodoviária plus a R$30–R$60 mini-schooner from Trindade.
scams.avoidance: Book Google 4.5+: Saveiros Soberanos, Escuna Mar Aberto, Escuna Saveiros R$70–R$120 Verify life jackets + Marinha registration sticker BEFORE boarding REFUSE 'private' / 'VIP' / 'islands access' upsells Pre-book 1–2 days ahead in high season Trindade: take R$8 local bus, NOT R$250 'speedboat'
scams.location: Paraty Marina (Largo do Rosário), Praia do Pontal pier, Cais do Cabral schooner pier, Centro Histórico tour-booking touts, hotel-concierge boat-tour desks
scams.tldr: Paraty Bay's flagship Passeio de Escuna schooner tour runs R$70–R$120 group with reputable Google 4.5+ operators (Saveiros Soberanos, Escuna Mar Aberto, Escuna Saveiros) — but Centro Histórico touts pitch 'private schooner R$500 per person' and 'VIP exclusive Lagoa Azul + Praia Vermelha R$800' for routes that are already standard stops, alongside unlicensed boats lacking life jackets or Marinha registration.

scams.name: Paraty Centro Histórico Restaurant Tourist-Menu & Couvert Bill-Padding
scams.description:
Paraty's Centro Histórico is a compact 8×6-block UNESCO cobblestone old town that's almost entirely pedestrian, dining-dense, and built around the Rua da Lapa and Rua Comendador José Luiz waterfront where every package-tour Brazilian visitor and every Rio day-tripper is funnelled through the same restaurant strip. That density supports a tourist-menu bill-padding pattern that runs around two consumer-protection facts most foreign visitors don't know: Brazilian law (Lei 13.419/2017) makes the 10% serviço charge optional, and INMETRO regulates pricing disclosure on menus and weighed items.

The Paraty trap menu starts with USD-only menus at the waterfront restaurants — Brazilian moqueca quoted at US$30+ when the same dish is R$70–R$110 at non-tourist spots, with the dollar conversion adding 10–15% on top of the existing markup. 'Couvert artístico' (the live-music cover charge) is layered at R$60–R$180 per person for a single guitarist when legitimate couvert for a real performer is R$15–R$35 disclosed before seating. Bottled 'água mineral' at R$22 vs the real R$6–R$12, undisclosed credit-card surcharges of 5–10% added at payment, and the bill-switcheroo where the printed receipt total doesn't match the card-charge amount round out the standard padding. The most expensive single play is 'lagosta peso variável' — a market-price lobster quoted at R$800–R$1,400 per kg with no weight shown before cooking, where a 1.5-kg lobster lands as a R$1,800 line item. Cachaça shots at R$80 are sold from house bottles when reputable artisanal cachaça runs R$25–R$50 at proper distilleries, and a R$600 'Paraty seafood platter for 2' typically delivers R$250 worth of fish padded with bread, palm hearts, and a couvert charge.

For travellers eating in Centro Histórico, the defense is to eat at authentic Paraty venues with menu prices in reais and to know the consumer-protection rules before sitting. Eat at authentic Paraty spots — Caminho do Ouro on the waterfront for traditional Caiçara cuisine (Google 4.7+, R$80–R$180 per meal), Banana da Terra on Rua Dr Samuel Costa for regional Brazilian (R$90–R$200), Quintal das Letras for vegetarian-friendly patio dining (R$60–R$140), Restaurante Sereia do Mar at Praia do Pontal for fish (R$70–R$150) — and before sitting, photograph the menu, confirm the couvert artístico amount per person and the credit-card surcharge in writing, and refuse any unordered couvert (bread, olive oil, palm hearts) since Brazilian Lei 13.419/2017 makes serviço optional and you can decline a 10% charge for poor service. Order 'água sem gás copo' (tap water in a glass, free) at most places. For weighed seafood, agree the weight in writing before cooking — fair 2026 prices are R$400–R$700 per kg for lobster and R$80–R$130 per kg for white fish. Skip USD-only menus entirely and ask for the real R$ amount. For cachaça, the proper Paraty experience is at the distilleries 5 km from Centro at R$8–R$25 a shot, not the R$80 tourist-restaurant pour. The Sunday afternoon Feira do Pescador fishmonger market at Praia do Pontal sells fresh-grilled fish meals at R$35–R$60 and is the budget locals' answer to the waterfront strip.
scams.avoidance: Eat: Caminho do Ouro, Banana da Terra, Quintal das Letras, Sereia do Mar BEFORE sitting confirm couvert / serviço / card surcharge in writing 'Serviço 10%' optional (Lei 13.419/2017); refuse if poor service Lobster: agree weight × R$400–R$700/kg in writing Sunday: 'feira do pescador' Praia do Pontal R$35–R$60
scams.location: Centro Histórico cobblestone street restaurants, Praia do Pontal waterfront dining, Rua da Lapa tourist-menu strip, Rua Comendador José Luiz dining row
scams.tldr: Paraty Centro Histórico waterfront restaurants on Rua da Lapa and Rua Comendador José Luiz post USD-only menus at 2–3× local prices, layer R$60–R$180 'couvert artístico' for a single guitarist (legitimate is R$15–R$35), present 'serviço 10%' as mandatory when Brazilian Lei 13.419/2017 makes it optional, and quote 'lagosta peso variável' market-price lobster at R$800–R$1,400 per kg without weight disclosed.

scams.name: Paraty Cachaça Distillery 'Premium Tasting' Commission Scam
scams.description:
Paraty is Brazil's historic centre for artisanal cachaça production, with multiple working distilleries dating to the Portuguese colonial era and IBRAC (Brazilian Cachaça Institute) certification on the country's most respected producers. Distillery visits are one of the destination's signature half-day cultural experiences, and the four reputable open-to-visitors stops — Engenho d'Ouro 5 km from Centro, Pedra Branca 8 km, Maria Izabel, and Coqueiro — are the right answer for both tasting and bottle purchases. The 2025 commission-tour ecosystem exploits visitor confusion between 'cachaça artesanal' (hand-distilled in copper alembics with fresh cane juice — the good stuff) and 'cachaça industrial' (column-distilled, skip), and between distillery-direct prices and Centro Histórico tourist-shop markups.

Real distillery prices are simple: Engenho d'Ouro R$30–R$60 entry (tour plus 4–6 tastings), Pedra Branca R$25–R$50, Maria Izabel R$35–R$70. Quality artisanal Paraty bottles run R$60–R$120 for Coqueiro 500ml, R$80–R$180 for Pedra Branca, R$150–R$300 for Engenho d'Ouro envelhecida (aged), and R$250–R$500 for top-shelf 5+ year amburana or bálsamo wood-aged. The trap menu starts with the hotel-concierge 'cachaça distillery tour combo R$350 per person' against a real DIY of R$50 round-trip Uber plus R$30–R$60 entry (R$80–R$110 per person). At the distillery itself, 'premium tasting flight R$200' duplicates what's already included in the standard entry. 'Master cachaça 12-year aged R$1,500 per bottle' inflates against legitimate R$400–R$800 from reputable producers, and the vintage-and-barrel-wood claims often don't survive a quick check. Centro Histórico tourist shops sell 'limited-edition Paraty cachaça US$80 per 200ml' for what's R$60–R$150 at the same producer's distillery counter. Layered on top: 'mandatory shipping fee R$200' for take-home bottles when Brazilian Correios is R$30–R$60 for one to two bottles, 'private chauffeur to 3 distilleries R$800' against R$60–R$80 Uber per leg, and 'cachaça master class R$400 per person' that turns out to be a 30-minute Centro talk when distillery tasting at R$30–R$60 covers equivalent education from people who actually distil.

For travellers planning a cachaça distillery day, the defense is to take Uber and pay distillery-direct. Take Uber from Centro to Engenho d'Ouro 5 km (R$50 round-trip with wait), Pedra Branca 8 km (R$80 round-trip), or Maria Izabel directly — pay R$25–R$70 entry that includes the tour and 4–6 tastings, and buy bottles at the distillery counter at R$60–R$300 (often 30–50% cheaper than Centro Histórico tourist shops); refuse every hotel-concierge 'distillery combo R$350 per person,' every distillery 'premium tasting flight R$200' (already included in entry), every 'master cachaça 12-year R$1,500 bottle' against the R$400–R$800 reputable price, every Centro tourist-shop 'limited-edition US$80 per 200ml,' and every 'mandatory shipping R$200' fee against the R$30–R$60 Correios reality. Stick to IBRAC-certified producers — Coqueiro, Pedra Branca, Engenho d'Ouro, Maria Izabel — and look for 'cachaça artesanal' or 'cachaça de alambique' on the label rather than industrial column-distilled. Pedra Branca is the most photogenic working distillery for travellers wanting to see the alembics in operation. For international bring-home, declare value honestly and use Correios with tracking; ICMS tax may apply on high-value shipments. Plan lunch around the Engenho d'Ouro restaurant (R$80–R$150) for traditional Caiçara cuisine — the half-day cultural visit is one of the better-value Paraty experiences when booked DIY.
scams.avoidance: Uber direct to Engenho d'Ouro R$50 round-trip; entry R$30–R$60 includes tasting Buy DIRECT at distillery (30–50% cheaper than Centro tourist shops) Reputable: Coqueiro, Pedra Branca, Engenho d'Ouro, Maria Izabel (IBRAC certified) Look for 'cachaça artesanal' / 'de alambique' label (skip industrial) Correios shipping R$30–R$60 for 1–2 bottles internationally
scams.location: Cachaça distillery tour stops outside Paraty Centro (Engenho d'Ouro, Pedra Branca, Maria Izabel), Centro Histórico cachaça shops, hotel-concierge cachaça-tour bookings
scams.tldr: Paraty's cachaça distilleries (Engenho d'Ouro, Pedra Branca, Maria Izabel, Coqueiro) charge R$25–R$70 entry including tour and 4–6 tastings — but Centro hotel concierges bundle 'distillery tour combos' at R$350 per person, Centro tourist shops sell 'limited-edition Paraty cachaça US$80 per 200ml' for what's R$60–R$150 at the producer's own door, and 'master cachaça 12-year aged R$1,500' bottles inflate against R$400–R$800 reputable pricing.

scams.name: Paraty Trindade & Angra Day-Trip Tour Commission Stops
scams.description:
Paraty sits on the Costa Verde almost exactly between two of the region's signature day-trip targets. Trindade — a tiny Caiçara beach village 35 km south, reachable on a R$8 local bus in 50 minutes — has four walk-from-centre beaches (Praia dos Ranchos, Cepilho, Praia do Cachadaço, Lagoa Azul) and the free Cachoeira do Tobogã natural-slide waterfall five minutes from the village. Angra dos Reis 50 km north on the Auto Viação Costa Verde bus is the ferry hub for Ilha Grande, the largest island on Brazil's southeast coast. Both are easy DIY days, and that's exactly the gap Centro Histórico tour-desks paper over with bundled commission-kickback packages.

Real prices keep the DIY anchor honest. Trindade is R$8 each way on the local bus (50 minutes, every 1–2 hours from Paraty Rodoviária) or R$80 each way by Uber, plus R$30–R$60 for a beach-hopping mini-schooner from Trindade pier if you want the offshore beaches. Angra is R$15–R$30 each way on the Auto Viação Costa Verde bus (50 km, one hour) plus a R$25–R$40 ferry to Ilha Grande, totalling R$80–R$140 round-trip Paraty-to-Ilha-Grande and best done as a two-day rather than a same-day trip. The trap menu starts with Centro Histórico touts selling 'Trindade + Angra combined day-trip R$600 per person' against a real DIY of R$80–R$160. The 'recommended driver + tour combo R$800' from your pousada concierge is the kickback variant. 'Private speedboat to Ilha Grande R$1,800 per person' is fictional against the legitimate R$25–R$40 ferry. 'Lagoa Azul exclusive Trindade access R$250' charges for what's already part of the standard Trindade beach-hopping route. 'Cachoeira do Tobogã private guide R$150' charges for a free public waterfall five minutes from Trindade centre. 'Mandatory ferry skip-the-line R$80' at Angra is fiction (no skip-the-line exists). Layered on top: a commission-restaurant lunch stop at R$200 per person added silently to the route, and tour-bus drivers detouring to commission cachaça shops on the BR-101 corridor where bottles cost two to three times the distillery price.

For travellers planning Trindade or Angra day-trips, the defense is the public bus and a flexible itinerary that doesn't try to do both in one day. For Trindade, take the local bus from Paraty Rodoviária at R$8 each way (or Uber R$80) and walk to the four village-centre beaches — Praia dos Ranchos, Cepilho, Praia do Cachadaço, Lagoa Azul — using a R$30–R$60 mini-schooner from Trindade pier if you want the offshore route; for Angra, take Costa Verde bus at R$15–R$30 plus the R$25–R$40 ferry to Ilha Grande as a two-day trip; refuse every 'Trindade + Angra combined R$600,' every 'private speedboat to Ilha Grande R$1,800,' every 'Lagoa Azul exclusive R$250,' every 'Cachoeira do Tobogã private guide R$150,' and every 'mandatory ferry skip-the-line R$80' as either commission stacking or outright fiction. Eat in Trindade at Restaurante Olho de Boi in the village centre (fresh fish, R$50–R$100) or Restaurante 7 Estrelas at Praia do Cepilho (R$60–R$120) rather than the 'commission-restaurant lunch stop' on a tour route. Buy your Angra ferry ticket at the terminal box office on the day at R$25–R$40 — there is no skip-the-line product, only legitimate boarding. If a tour-bus driver detours to a 'recommended cachaça shop' on the BR-101, refuse to enter; the real distillery purchases happen at Engenho d'Ouro and Pedra Branca closer to Paraty Centro at half the price.
scams.avoidance: Trindade local bus R$8 each way (50 min); or Uber R$80 At Trindade, walk village (5-min) or mini-schooner R$30–R$60 Ilha Grande: Costa Verde bus + Angra ferry = R$80–R$140 round-trip Tobogã waterfall is FREE public; refuse 'private guide R$150' Eat: Restaurante Olho de Boi or 7 Estrelas R$50–R$120
scams.location: Centro Histórico tour-booking touts, hotel-concierge day-trip desks, Trindade beach village (35 km south of Paraty Centro), Angra dos Reis schooner connections, BR-101 highway day-trip routes
scams.tldr: Paraty is the obvious base for Trindade (35 km south, beach village) and Angra dos Reis (50 km north, the gateway to Ilha Grande), and Centro Histórico tour-desks bundle 'Trindade + Angra combined day-trip R$600 per person' against a R$80–R$160 DIY total via R$8 local bus and R$25–R$40 ferry — a 4–7× markup that's pure commission stacking.

scams.name: Paraty Pousada Carnaval & FLIP Festival Cancel-and-Relist Fraud
scams.description:
Paraty's two peak booking windows — Carnaval in late February or early March and FLIP, the Festa Literária Internacional de Paraty in late July — concentrate Brazil's domestic and literary tourism into a single UNESCO town with limited Centro Histórico stock. FLIP alone draws 30,000+ attendees as Brazil's premier literary festival, and accommodation rates run four to eight times normal across both windows. That pricing pressure on a small inventory creates exactly the cancel-and-relist conditions seen in Rio, Búzios, and Ouro Preto Carnaval, plus the WhatsApp PIX fraud pattern that targets last-minute international bookers.

The mechanic spans the booking funnel and the on-arrival door. Booking.com and Airbnb 'phantom listings' use stolen photos of Centro Histórico colonial pousadas — the traveller pays in advance, arrives, and finds no property at the address. Confirmed-booking cancellations land 30–60 days before Carnaval or FLIP, with the host citing a 'pousada emergency' before re-listing the same unit at three to five times the original price (the platform refunds the original payment, but you're stuck a month from travel with prices doubled). WhatsApp 'private Centro Histórico apartment for FLIP R$3,500/night' offers demand 100% PIX upfront — Brazilian PIX is irreversible once cleared, and the listing disappears the moment payment confirms. A 'colonial Centro pousada' booking turns out to be 1–2 kilometres outside Centro in suburban Paraty (always verify on Google Maps before paying). On-arrival bait-and-switch downgrades a confirmed Centro unit to an inferior room, and 'cleaning deposit R$600 cash on arrival' never returns at checkout. The festival overlay adds 'mandatory FLIP package R$4,500 for 4 nights' (which covers nothing beyond the standard room rate), 'reserved festival access R$800 per person' (FLIP has free public sessions and ticketed mesas at R$60–R$120 sold officially at flip.org.br), and 'pousada inaccessible by car R$300' porter charges for wheeling luggage 200 metres on cobblestone (legitimate porter help is R$30–R$50 if you genuinely need it).

For travellers planning a Paraty trip during Carnaval or FLIP, the defense is to book six to nine months ahead at recognised pousadas paid by credit card, and to verify everything 72 hours before arrival. Book Paraty Carnaval or FLIP six to nine months ahead via Booking.com or Hotels.com platform payment at recognised pousadas — Pousada do Sandi (Centro Histórico boutique, 4-star, Google 4.7+), Pousada Literária (FLIP-themed, R$800–R$1,500/night), Casa Turquesa (luxury boutique), or Sandi Hotel — never PIX-transfer to a WhatsApp 'apartment owner,' verify the pousada name on Google Maps and Tripadvisor before paying to confirm it's inside the 8×6-block Centro Histórico, and refuse 'mandatory FLIP package R$4,500,' 'reserved festival access R$800,' and on-arrival 'cleaning deposit R$600 cash' demands. Confirm your booking by direct phone call 72 hours before arrival, with a written overbooking-relocation commitment if the pousada has any history of cancellations. For FLIP, buy festival access only at flip.org.br — free public sessions plus R$60–R$120 mesas — and skip every reseller. Centro Histórico is fully cobblestone Portuguese colonial paving, so pack a rolling case with inflated tyres or a backpack rather than handling 'porter R$300' upsells. For budget travellers, base in Trindade 35 km south at simpler pousadas at R$200–R$400/night and bus into Paraty for events. DEAT Tourist Police Paraty +55 24 3371 1334 takes booking-fraud denuncias within 48 hours.
scams.avoidance: Book 6–9 months ahead via Booking.com / hotel chains Reputable: Pousada do Sandi, Pousada Literária, Casa Turquesa, Sandi Hotel AVOID Airbnb peak-season; NEVER PIX-transfer to WhatsApp sellers Cross-reference pousada on Google Maps (verify within Centro 8×6-block zone) FLIP official: free sessions + R$60–R$120 mesas at flip.org.br
scams.location: Paraty pousada Booking.com / Airbnb listings, Carnaval (Feb–Mar) booking window, FLIP literary festival (late July) accommodations, WhatsApp 'private apartment' Centro Histórico offers
scams.tldr: Paraty accommodation rates spike 4–8× during Carnaval (late February or early March) and FLIP (Festa Literária Internacional de Paraty, late July, 30,000+ attendees), drawing Booking.com/Airbnb cancel-and-relist plays where R$450/night confirmed bookings get cancelled 30–60 days out and re-listed at R$1,800–R$3,500, plus WhatsApp 'private Centro apartment' offers demanding 100% PIX upfront and 'mandatory FLIP package R$4,500 for 4 nights' upsells.
